fact: On 18 March 2025 armed police stormed the Risaala Media station in Mogadishu, took it off-air and arrested five named journalists without a court warrant, after it was first to report the bombing of the president's convoy; the document gives no law.

Defenders Coalition Somalia, a Somali civil-society group, with DefendDefenders, criticised in a joint UN review submission the Official Information Bill approved by the Council of Ministers in March 2024, for broad confidentiality and national-security exemptions, no independent oversight and drafting in secrecy; the document is dated 28 October 2025.

Amnesty International says journalists in Somalia were subjected to arbitrary arrests and prosecution as the government stepped up attempts to censor reporting on insecurity, corruption and forced evictions.

Geeska Freedom Centre reports that police arrested journalist Abdukadir Abukar Ali on 25 June 2026 after he published a video questioning the fairness of a trial, accusing him of insulting judicial institutions; he was bailed on 28 June with charges pending.

Geeska Freedom Centre reports that police arrested Iftiimiye TV reporter Mohamed Ali Mohamud on 26 June 2026 after he reported a police officer's claim that senior officers had unlawfully suspended his salary, and held him three days without charge.

Geeska Freedom Centre reports that NISA officers forcibly disappeared Xogbile founder Mascuud Warsame on 30 June 2026, an outlet that has published reporting critical of the South West State administration, and that he remained in custody without charge.

WardheerNews states that on 2 March 2025 access to its own site was blocked on Hormuud Telecommunications' network across Mogadishu, Hirshabelle, Galmudug, South West State and Jubaland, which it attributes to the government.
WardheerNews states that political commentator and journalist Ali Adan Mumin was arrested on 1 March 2025 on charges of threatening national security and defaming government officials.

RSF reports that the National Union of Somali Journalists, through its Secretary General, criticised the draft Penal Code adopted by the Council of Ministers in December 2025 as risking a more restrictive environment for independent journalism and drawn up without meaningful consultation.
